text.en: One day little Shambhu was walking through the forest with his father. They sat down in the cool shade of a huge mango tree, which was home to birds, squirrels, monkeys and many other animals. Shambhu saw a monkey eating a mango and throwing away the seed. That small moment shows how plants, animals and we depend on each other.

We bring some animals and plants into our homes, and some start living in our homes on their own. Sometimes we share our home with them happily, but sometimes we do not like them in our home. We take care of the animals and plants in our homes by giving them water, food and shelter. Some animals, birds and insects visit our homes without being invited. We can talk with a partner about which ones come, why they come, how we feel and which we like. Even when we do not like an animal or are scared of it, we must not hurt it. Animals generally do not hurt others unless they feel threatened by us.
The mango tree was home to birds, squirrels, monkeys and many other animals. A tree can be a house for many living things. Shambhu saw a monkey eating a mango and throwing out the seed. His father explained that a new plant would grow from this seed. This is how animals and plants help each other. Shambhu picked up a mango that had fallen from the tree and said that he had also got a mango. His father said we get fruits and vegetables from plants, and also medicines, fibre for clothes and wood for our houses.
Plants give us many things. They give us shade, fruits, fresh air, medicine, wood and fibre. Plants also give shelter to animals, and give food to animals. Cotton and jute are plant fibres that we use for making clothes and ropes, and wood from trees is used to make doors, tables and houses. Because plants give us so much, we should plant trees, water them and not break their branches or pluck flowers needlessly. Think of a mango tree: its fruit feeds us, its leaves give shade, and its branches hold birds' nests.
We give care, protection, food and shelter to animals and plants, and we get many things from them as well. From cows, buffaloes and goats we get milk and loving company. That is why we respect these animals and treat them with kindness, care and compassion. Animals and plants depend on each other too. They need each other for food and shelter. Animals help plants by dispersing, which means spreading, their seeds. They also make the soil fertile by their waste, which means the soil becomes rich so that plants grow well. This helps plants to grow and spread near and far.
Thousands of trees are planted by squirrels by accident. They bury nuts and then forget where they hid them. The buried nuts grow into new trees. This is one way animals and plants keep harmony and balance in nature. Harmony means living together peacefully, helping and not harming each other. When we put out water for birds in summer, or avoid breaking nests, we are keeping harmony too. Remember: every living thing, big or small, has a place in our world and needs our kindness.
We can choose an animal or bird we see often, such as a goat, cow, dog, cat, crow, pigeon, sparrow, parrot or duck, and watch it closely, perhaps keeping a bowl of water and some grains for it. We can note its name, where and when we saw it, how it moves, what sounds it makes and what it eats, and share the story with our classmates. In the ant activity we place three kinds of food, a sweet like sugar or jaggery, something fried like a papad and something cooked like rice, a foot apart on the floor and watch which one the ants go to first. We can make friends with a plant. When we are happy or sad we can go to our plant friend and share our feelings. We should care for the plant, and animals need our care too.
Valparai is a small town in Tamil Nadu. All through the school year, children and teachers look for and record the birds that come to their town. In the cold winter months, a bird called the Grey Wagtail (Vaalatti kuruvi in Tamil) arrives from the mountains to the warmer parts of India, and stays for a few months. When the first Grey Wagtails arrive, the children and teachers welcome them with posters and share sweets with everyone. This shows that we can love and welcome the birds and animals who share our world, and live in harmony with them.

problem.en: How does a mango seed become a new tree with the help of an animal?

text.en: A monkey eats a mango and throws away the seed.

why.en: The seed is the part from which a new plant can grow.

text.en: The seed lands on the soil and, with water and sunlight, starts to sprout.

why.en: A seed needs soil, water and sunlight.

text.en: The sprout grows into a new mango tree. This is how animals help plants by spreading seeds.

why.en: The animal helped to spread the seed, a process called dispersal.

problem.en: Do the ant activity: which food will the ants go to first?

text.en: Place a sweet, a fried and a cooked food in a line, a foot apart.

why.en: Placing the foods apart lets us see which one is chosen.

text.en: Make a guess before you watch: which one will they come to first?

why.en: A guess is a prediction we can check.

text.en: Watch for some time, then say what happened and why you think so.

why.en: We learn by watching carefully, and ants like sweet foods.

prompt.en: Tell a friend how we depend on plants and animals, and how they depend on us.

requiredIdeas.en: Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood, fibre and fresh air
Animals give us milk and companionship and help plants by spreading seeds
We give them food, water, shelter and care
We should not hurt animals or plants

commonMisconceptions.en: Plants and animals do not need us
We can hurt animals we do not like

points.en: Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood, fibre and fresh air.
Animals give us milk and company and help plants by spreading seeds and making the soil fertile.
We care for animals and plants by giving them food, water and shelter.
We must not hurt animals even if we are scared of them.
Squirrels plant trees by forgetting where they buried nuts.
In Valparai, children welcome the Grey Wagtail birds each winter.
